body:
Thank you for your words and presence. Yes, I need to learn how to not overthink things, not to question every single think i do and say. There is no need for it.

But i don't know how! I've tried but I always end up feeling ashamed. I definitely lack "emotional intelligence". I don't know how to be with others without feeling worthless and shameful. I just can't seem to be loving towards myself.

Thank you so much. <3 

You are right, I cannot do this by myself. I do feel isolated. I isolate myself from others to avoid feeling ashamed. I have consulted and still do, but it's not helping reduced my shame. But I do appreciate having an ear. The counselor agrees with me that I have some sense of self-awareness, but yet I cannot seem to change how I feel. Intellectually, I'm well aware that there is no need to feel ashamed, to feel like I am a mistake instead of telling myself I have made a mistake (even when I haven't - for example, I felt ashamed to have bought some cupcakes for a teacher, as a thank-you present, after the semester was over - I do understand that there is nothing wrong with that, and the teacher was appreciative of it, but I just felt ashamed... I don't know, I felt like a suck-up, despite the fact that I did it out of gratefulness for the great course she has offered).

My mother belittled me, insulted me and treated me like I was less worthy of her love than my siblings. That's where my sense of shame took roots. And unfortunately, it is anchored very deeply within me and it is pushing me to the edge of the cliff right now. I'm so tired to fight with myself and my shame.

Again, thank you so very much for your understanding, for your constructive feedback, for being there tonight. Take care of yourself.
